description:
## Purpose
Notes item. It holds the owner's decisions and the order of the five steps. It is never implemented itself; it closes when every step is done, dropped with the owner's reason, or blocked on a named owner gate.

## Problem
`benchbox run` has no timeout. Time bounds are scattered: UAT kills each cell from outside (tests/uat/timeouts.py, 600 s default); dsqgen has hard-coded 30 s and 300 s limits; the TPC-DS runner checks a 300 s query limit only after the query returns; plan capture abandons a thread after 30 s; engines each have their own setting; `utils/timeout_manager.py` and `ResourceLimitsConfig` hold timers with no caller. The runner has no way to stop a run except for throughput streams.

## Owner's request
"We should have a generalized run timeout (e.g. `--timeout SECONDS`) that applies to any type of run; not jsut data generation but also benchmark executions." Earlier: "We do need to **ALLOW** a user to specify a datagen timeout even though we MUST NOT enforce a default timeout."

## Settled semantics (owner, choice dialog, 2026-11-20)
- Name: "`--timeout SECONDS`, whole seconds only, on `run`, `run-official` and `datagen`"; `timeout_seconds` in the MCP run tool and the Python API; `execution.timeout_seconds` in the config file.
- No default: unset means BenchBox never stops a run on its own.
- Scope: "one clock for the whole invocation, from start to exit: generate, load and execute together. The existing narrower settings (stream, statement) stay as tighter limits inside it."
- At the limit: "BenchBox asks everything to stop (cancels where it can, kills generator processes). If the run has not stopped after a fixed 30-second grace, it writes what it has and exits. So the hard bound is the limit plus 30 seconds."
- After a timeout: "keep a partial result, marked as timed out with the phase and query reached. It can never be official, published, submitted or ranked. Data generated by a stopped generator is not marked complete and is not reused."
- Exit code 124.

## Delivery
Owner: "five pull requests, one per step, each merged before the next starts. Nothing is stacked. I work them in order without stopping between them unless a gate fails." ('I' is the agent.)

## Order
1. tpc-generation-no-default-timeout-optional-user-timeout-20261120: the deadline, `--timeout` on every surface, generators, boundaries, backstop, exit code, partial result, decision record.
2. run-timeout-execution-phases-20261120: power, throughput and maintenance execution; native cancel; execution defaults removed; timing proof.
3. run-timeout-remote-cleanup-20261120: remote statement and session cleanup on cloud platforms, stub-verified, with a warning.
4. run-timeout-uat-cells-20261120: UAT cells pass `--timeout`; outside kill at cell limit plus 60 s.
5. run-timeout-remove-unused-timers-20261120: remove timers with no caller; plan capture on the deadline; one kill helper.
Then tpc-generation-duration-estimate-20261120 (separate: measurement runs, table to the owner, then the estimate and the warning when `--timeout` is shorter than it).

## Other decisions
- No new CI check against hard-coded timeouts (owner: "no new CI check"). The remaining literals for container start-up, health checks and credential calls stay.
- Cloud: "build the remote cleanup, verify it with stubbed clients only, and print a warning on cloud platforms that remote work may continue after a timeout until a live check has been done. No live cloud runs."

## Gates that stop at the owner
- Step 2: if the before-and-after medians differ by more than 2%.
- Estimate: the measured table, before any estimate figure is committed.
- Any value not already chosen above (for example a config default, a message that states a limit other than the user's, a new exit code).

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text the owner has not already chosen is shown to the owner before it is committed. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
